title: Large Repositories
description: Manage Git repositories with gigabytes of history, large binary assets, or thousands of contributors without sacrificing performance.

data.text: Large repositories stress Git's default assumptions about network transfers, disk usage, and operation speed. Git was designed for text-based source code, not media files or decade-long histories. When a repository grows beyond a few gigabytes, you need deliberate strategies to keep it usable.

items: Clones take minutes instead of seconds.
Git commands like `git status` and `git log` noticeably lag.
Disk usage on CI runners spikes and slows pipelines.
Pushes and fetches transfer megabytes of unchanged data.

data.text: Git Large File Storage (LFS) replaces large files in your working tree with lightweight pointer files. The actual binaries live on a separate LFS server. This keeps the main repository small while preserving the developer experience of checking out large assets.

data.title: Track large files with Git LFS
data.code:
# Install Git LFS (one-time setup)
git lfs install

# Track specific file types
git lfs track "*.psd"
git lfs track "*.zip"

# Commit the tracking rules
git add .gitattributes
git commit -m "chore: track design assets with LFS"

data.text: A shallow clone downloads only the most recent commits. For CI and one-off debugging, this can cut clone time from minutes to seconds. The trade-off is that you cannot push from a shallow clone and some commands like `git blame` have limited history.

data.title: Clone with limited depth
data.code:
git clone --depth=50 https://github.com/example/large-repo.git
cd large-repo

# Fetch more history later if needed
git fetch --depth=200

data.title: LFS bandwidth is not free
data.text: Git LFS hosting costs money on platforms like GitHub and GitLab for heavy usage. Monitor LFS bandwidth and enforce file type filters so developers do not accidentally commit massive binaries.

Regular maintenance prevents gradual bloat. Run `git gc` periodically, use `git repack` after large deletions, and monitor `.git` directory size. For repositories that accumulate many stale branches, prune references aggressively.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Large binaries belong in Git LFS, not in the main object store.
Shallow clones speed up CI and ad-hoc debugging.
Monitor repository size and run maintenance commands regularly.
Combine LFS, shallow clones, and pruning for large-repo health.
